part1.tip: Test-takers often jump to D ("running on the path") because it's an active-sounding verb, but nothing in a normal park photo confirms running specifically — "taking a walk" is the safer, more general description that photos usually support.
part1.tipVn: Nhiều người dễ chọn D ("running on the path") vì nghe có vẻ là một hành động chủ động, nhưng ảnh công viên bình thường không thể xác nhận cụ thể là đang chạy — "taking a walk" là mô tả an toàn và tổng quát hơn mà ảnh thường minh chứng được.
part1.tipTh: ผู้เข้าสอบมักรีบเลือก D ("running on the path") เพราะฟังดูเป็นกริยาที่กระตือรือร้น แต่ไม่มีอะไรในภาพสวนสาธารณะทั่วไปยืนยันการวิ่งโดยเฉพาะ — "taking a walk" เป็นคำอธิบายที่ปลอดภัยกว่าและทั่วไปกว่าที่ภาพมักสนับสนุนได้
part1.tipZh: 考生常常急著選 D（"running on the path"）因為聽起來是個主動的動詞，但一般公園照片並無法特別確認正在跑步——"taking a walk" 是更安全、更籠統的描述，通常也更符合照片內容。
part1.tipFr: Les candidats sautent souvent sur D ("running on the path") car c'est un verbe qui sonne actif, mais rien dans une photo de parc normale ne confirme spécifiquement la course — "taking a walk" est la description plus sûre et générale que les photos confirment habituellement.
part1.tipKo: 응시자들은 흔히 D("running on the path")를 선택합니다. 능동적으로 들리는 동사이기 때문이지만, 일반적인 공원 사진만으로는 구체적으로 뛰고 있다는 것을 확인할 수 없습니다 — "taking a walk"가 사진이 보통 뒷받침하는 더 안전하고 일반적인 설명입니다.
part1.tipJa: 受験者はしばしば D（"running on the path"）に飛びつきますが、これは動作的に聞こえる動詞だからです。しかし普通の公園の写真では走っていると具体的に確認できるものはありません — "taking a walk" の方が写真が通常裏付けるより安全で一般的な説明です。
part1.tipId: Peserta tes sering langsung memilih D ("running on the path") karena terdengar seperti kata kerja aktif, tetapi tidak ada yang mengonfirmasi berlari secara spesifik dalam foto taman biasa — "taking a walk" adalah deskripsi yang lebih aman dan umum yang biasanya didukung oleh foto.
part1.tipEl: Οι εξεταζόμενοι συχνά πηδούν στο D ("running on the path") επειδή ακούγεται σαν ενεργητικό ρήμα, αλλά τίποτα σε μια συνηθισμένη φωτογραφία πάρκου δεν επιβεβαιώνει συγκεκριμένα το τρέξιμο — το "taking a walk" είναι η πιο ασφαλής, γενικότερη περιγραφή που συνήθως υποστηρίζουν οι φωτογραφίες.
part1.tipEs: Los examinados suelen saltar a D ("running on the path") porque suena como un verbo activo, pero nada en una foto normal de parque confirma correr específicamente — "taking a walk" es la descripción más segura y general que las fotos suelen respaldar.

part1.tip: B ("typing on his laptop") is a tempting trap because a laptop is plausible in an office scene, but if only one person could be doing that specific action, it's a weaker match than a general statement like "having a business meeting" that covers the whole group.
part1.tipVn: B ("typing on his laptop") là bẫy hấp dẫn vì laptop hợp lý trong bối cảnh văn phòng, nhưng nếu chỉ một người có thể đang làm hành động cụ thể đó, nó sẽ kém phù hợp hơn một câu tổng quát như "having a business meeting" bao quát cả nhóm.
part1.tipTh: B ("typing on his laptop") เป็นกับดักที่น่าดึงดูดเพราะแล็ปท็อปเป็นไปได้ในฉากออฟฟิศ แต่ถ้ามีเพียงคนเดียวที่อาจกำลังทำการกระทำเฉพาะนั้น มันจะเข้ากันได้น้อยกว่าประโยคทั่วไปอย่าง "having a business meeting" ที่ครอบคลุมทั้งกลุ่ม
part1.tipZh: B（"typing on his laptop"）是誘人的陷阱，因為辦公室場景中出現筆電很合理，但如果只有一個人可能在做那個特定動作，就不如像 "having a business meeting" 這種涵蓋整個群體的籠統敘述更貼切。
part1.tipFr: B ("typing on his laptop") est un piège tentant car un ordinateur portable est plausible dans une scène de bureau, mais si une seule personne pouvait faire cette action précise, c'est une correspondance plus faible qu'un énoncé général comme "having a business meeting" couvrant tout le groupe.

part1.tipId: B ("typing on his laptop") adalah jebakan yang menggoda karena laptop masuk akal dalam adegan kantor, tetapi jika hanya satu orang yang bisa melakukan tindakan spesifik itu, itu adalah kecocokan yang lebih lemah dibandingkan pernyataan umum seperti "having a business meeting" yang mencakup seluruh kelompok.
part1.tipEl: Το B ("typing on his laptop") είναι μια δελεαστική παγίδα επειδή ένα λάπτοπ είναι εύλογο σε μια σκηνή γραφείου, αλλά αν μόνο ένα άτομο θα μπορούσε να κάνει αυτή τη συγκεκριμένη ενέργεια, ταιριάζει λιγότερο από μια γενική δήλωση όπως το "having a business meeting" που καλύπτει όλη την ομάδα.
part1.tipEs: B ("typing on his laptop") es una trampa tentadora porque una laptop es plausible en una escena de oficina, pero si solo una persona podría estar haciendo esa acción específica, es una coincidencia más débil que un enunciado general como "having a business meeting" que cubre a todo el grupo.

part1.tip: "Changing the tire" (D) is easily confused with "putting air into the tire" (A) — both involve a car and a tire, but changing implies removing/replacing the whole tire, while putting air in is a much smaller, different action; watch the specific verb closely.
part1.tipVn: "Changing the tire" (D) rất dễ nhầm với "putting air into the tire" (A) — cả hai đều liên quan đến xe và bánh xe, nhưng changing nghĩa là tháo/thay cả bánh, còn putting air in chỉ là hành động nhỏ hơn nhiều và khác hẳn; hãy chú ý kỹ động từ cụ thể.
part1.tipTh: "Changing the tire" (D) มักสับสนกับ "putting air into the tire" (A) — ทั้งสองเกี่ยวข้องกับรถและยาง แต่ changing หมายถึงการถอด/เปลี่ยนยางทั้งเส้น ในขณะที่ putting air in เป็นการกระทำที่เล็กกว่ามากและต่างกัน — จับตาดูกริยาเฉพาะให้ดี
part1.tipZh: "Changing the tire"（D）很容易與 "putting air into the tire"（A）混淆——兩者都涉及汽車和輪胎，但 changing 意味著拆卸/更換整個輪胎，而 putting air in 則是規模小得多、完全不同的動作；請仔細留意具體的動詞。
part1.tipFr: "Changing the tire" (D) est facilement confondu avec "putting air into the tire" (A) — les deux impliquent une voiture et un pneu, mais changer implique de retirer/remplacer tout le pneu, alors que gonfler est une action bien plus petite et différente ; surveillez de près le verbe précis.
part1.tipKo: "Changing the tire"(D)는 "putting air into the tire"(A)와 혼동하기 쉽습니다 — 둘 다 차와 타이어에 관련되지만, changing은 타이어 전체를 떼어내고 교체하는 것을 뜻하고, putting air in은 훨씬 작고 다른 동작입니다 — 정확한 동사를 주의 깊게 살펴보세요.

part1.tipId: "Changing the tire" (D) mudah tertukar dengan "putting air into the tire" (A) — keduanya melibatkan mobil dan ban, tetapi changing berarti melepas/mengganti seluruh ban, sedangkan memompa udara adalah tindakan yang jauh lebih kecil dan berbeda; perhatikan baik-baik kata kerja spesifiknya.
part1.tipEl: Το "changing the tire" (D) συγχέεται εύκολα με το "putting air into the tire" (A) — και τα δύο αφορούν ένα αυτοκίνητο και ένα λάστιχο, αλλά η αλλαγή σημαίνει αφαίρεση/αντικατάσταση ολόκληρου του λάστιχου, ενώ το φούσκωμα είναι μια πολύ μικρότερη, διαφορετική ενέργεια — παρακολουθήστε προσεκτικά το συγκεκριμένο ρήμα.
part1.tipEs: "Changing the tire" (D) se confunde fácilmente con "putting air into the tire" (A) — ambos implican un auto y una llanta, pero cambiar implica quitar/reemplazar toda la llanta, mientras que poner aire es una acción mucho más pequeña y distinta; observa de cerca el verbo específico.

part1.tipZh: "Cooking the fish"（C）在釣魚場景中聽起來合理，但把剛釣到魚後的那一刻（取下魚鉤）與之後不相關的活動混為一談——請將句子與圖中所示動作的確切階段對應起來。
part1.tipFr: "Cooking the fish" (C) semble plausible pour une scène de pêche, mais confond le moment juste après la prise (retirer l'hameçon) avec une activité ultérieure sans rapport — faites correspondre l'énoncé à l'étape précise de l'action montrée.
part1.tipKo: "Cooking the fish"(C)는 낚시 장면에 그럴듯하게 들리지만, 물고기를 잡은 직후 순간(낚싯바늘 빼기)을 이후의 무관한 활동과 혼동한 것입니다 — 문장을 사진에 나타난 동작의 정확한 단계에 맞추세요.
part1.tipJa: "Cooking the fish"（C）は釣りの場面ではもっともらしく聞こえますが、釣った直後の瞬間（フックを外す）と、その後の無関係な活動を混同しています — 文を、示されている動作の正確な段階に一致させましょう。
part1.tipId: "Cooking the fish" (C) terdengar masuk akal untuk adegan memancing, tetapi mencampuradukkan momen tepat setelah menangkap (melepas kail) dengan aktivitas berikutnya yang tidak berhubungan — cocokkan pernyataan dengan tahap pasti dari tindakan yang ditunjukkan.
part1.tipEl: Το "cooking the fish" (C) ακούγεται εύλογο για μια σκηνή ψαρέματος, αλλά συγχέει τη στιγμή αμέσως μετά το πιάσιμο (αφαίρεση του αγκίστρου) με μια μεταγενέστερη, άσχετη δραστηριότητα — ταιριάξτε την πρόταση με το ακριβές στάδιο της ενέργειας που φαίνεται.
part1.tipEs: "Cooking the fish" (C) suena plausible para una escena de pesca, pero confunde el momento justo después de la captura (quitar el anzuelo) con una actividad posterior no relacionada — haz coincidir el enunciado con la etapa precisa de la acción mostrada.

Hi everyone, thanks for meeting with me today. (83) I'd like announce a few changes in our health and safety policy that are designed to conform to the new government regulations. Firstly, we can no longer work a shift longer than six hours without taking a one-hour break. We'll be using a clock-in system that is automated to send you a text message once you reach six hours. You will also wear a device that monitors your time on the shift. (84) It's a very simple device, you just attach it to your work belt and it will do the rest, so you won't need any training with that. (85) Sharing helmets and work boots is also now prohibited. You will have to buy your own equipment, and then later you can claim the money back on your tax return.
83. B. to conform to government
ตามคำพูดของผู้พูด ทำไมจึงมีการเปลี่ยนแปลงนี้?
A. รัฐบาลนำบริษัทขึ้นศาล
B. เพื่อให้เป็นไปตามข้อกำหนดของรัฐบาล
C. เพื่อจัดตั้งสภาแรงงานใหม่
D. เพื่อจัดการเรื่องการจ่ายค่าจ้างที่ต่ำลง

แปลประโยคที่มีคำสำคัญ
(83)ฉันอยากจะประกาศการเปลี่ยนแปลงบางอย่างในนโยบายด้านสุขภาพและความปลอดภัยของเรา ซึ่งออกแบบมาเพื่อให้สอดคล้องกับข้อกำหนดใหม่ของรัฐบาล

บันทึก
- คำถามข้อมูลทั่วไป -> ข้อมูลมักอยู่ในตอนต้น
- conform to sth: สอดคล้องกับสิ่งใดสิ่งหนึ่ง
- enact a law: ประกาศใช้กฎหมาย
84. A. the new system requires no training
ผู้พูดหมายความว่าอย่างไรเมื่อพูดว่า "มันเป็นอุปกรณ์ที่เรียบง่ายมาก คุณแค่ติดมันไว้ที่เข็มขัดทำงานของคุณและมันจะทำที่เหลือ ดังนั้นคุณไม่จำเป็นต้องรับการฝึกอบรมใดๆกับมัน"?

D. ทุกคนต้องได้รับการฝึกอบรม

แปลประโยคที่มีคำสำคัญ
(84)มันเป็นอุปกรณ์ที่เรียบง่ายมาก คุณแค่ติดมันไว้ที่เข็มขัดทำงานของคุณ และมันจะทำที่เหลือ ดังนั้นคุณไม่จำเป็นต้องรับการฝึกอบรมใดๆกับมัน

C. รองเท้าและหมวกนิรภัยของตัวเอง
D. แผนการเงินใหม่

แปลประโยคที่มีคำสำคัญ
(85)การใช้หมวกนิรภัยและรองเท้าทำงานร่วมกันก็ถูกห้ามด้วย คุณจะต้องซื้ออุปกรณ์ของตัวเอง

part5.tip: "Considering" is the classic trap here — it sounds close in meaning to "except" but actually means "taking into account", the opposite direction of exclusion the sentence needs; always check whether the sentence is excluding something or factoring it in.
part5.tipVn: "Considering" là bẫy kinh điển ở đây — nghe có vẻ gần nghĩa với "except" nhưng thực ra có nghĩa "xét đến", ngược hướng với sự loại trừ mà câu cần; luôn kiểm tra xem câu đang loại trừ điều gì đó hay đang tính đến nó.
part5.tipTh: "Considering" คือกับดักคลาสสิกที่นี่ — ฟังดูใกล้เคียงกับ "except" แต่จริงๆ หมายถึง "คำนึงถึง" ทิศทางตรงข้ามกับการยกเว้นที่ประโยคต้องการ — ตรวจสอบเสมอว่าประโยคกำลังยกเว้นบางสิ่งหรือกำลังนำมาพิจารณา
part5.tipZh: "Considering" 是這裡的經典陷阱——聽起來與 "except" 意思相近，但實際上意思是「將……納入考量」，與句子所需的排除方向恰恰相反；務必檢查句子是在排除某事還是在考慮某事。
part5.tipFr: "Considering" est le piège classique ici — il sonne proche en sens de "except" mais signifie en réalité "en tenant compte de", la direction opposée à l'exclusion dont la phrase a besoin ; vérifiez toujours si la phrase exclut quelque chose ou en tient compte.
part5.tipKo: "Considering"는 여기서 전형적인 함정입니다 — "except"와 의미가 비슷하게 들리지만 실제로는 "고려하여"라는 뜻으로, 문장이 필요로 하는 배제와는 반대 방향입니다 — 문장이 무언가를 배제하는지 아니면 고려하는지 항상 확인하세요.
part5.tipJa: "Considering" はここでの典型的な罠です — "except" に意味が近く聞こえますが、実際は「考慮に入れて」という意味で、文が必要とする除外とは逆方向です — 文が何かを除外しているのか、考慮に入れているのか常に確認しましょう。
part5.tipId: "Considering" adalah jebakan klasik di sini — terdengar mirip artinya dengan "except" tetapi sebenarnya berarti "mempertimbangkan", arah yang berlawanan dari pengecualian yang dibutuhkan kalimat; selalu periksa apakah kalimat itu mengecualikan sesuatu atau memperhitungkannya.
part5.tipEl: Το "considering" είναι η κλασική παγίδα εδώ — ακούγεται κοντά στη σημασία του "except" αλλά στην πραγματικότητα σημαίνει "λαμβάνοντας υπόψη", την αντίθετη κατεύθυνση από τον αποκλεισμό που χρειάζεται η πρόταση — ελέγχετε πάντα αν η πρόταση αποκλείει κάτι ή το λαμβάνει υπόψη.
part5.tipEs: "Considering" es la trampa clásica aquí — suena cercano en significado a "except" pero en realidad significa "teniendo en cuenta", la dirección opuesta a la exclusión que necesita la oración; siempre revisa si la oración excluye algo o lo toma en cuenta.

part5.tip: "Himself" is the most common wrong pick here because learners assume any pronoun matching the subject must be reflexive — but a reflexive pronoun only fits at a clause's end or right after the subject, never right before a noun like "diagnosis".
part5.tipVn: "Himself" là lựa chọn sai phổ biến nhất ở đây vì người học thường nghĩ đại từ khớp với chủ ngữ phải là phản thân — nhưng đại từ phản thân chỉ phù hợp ở cuối mệnh đề hoặc ngay sau chủ ngữ, không bao giờ đứng ngay trước danh từ như "diagnosis".
part5.tipTh: "Himself" เป็นตัวเลือกผิดที่พบบ่อยที่สุดที่นี่ เพราะผู้เรียนมักคิดว่าสรรพนามที่ตรงกับประธานต้องเป็นสรรพนามสะท้อน — แต่สรรพนามสะท้อนเหมาะสมเฉพาะที่ท้ายอนุประโยคหรือทันทีหลังประธาน ไม่เคยอยู่หน้าคำนามอย่าง "diagnosis"
part5.tipZh: "Himself" 是這裡最常見的錯誤選項，因為學習者常以為與主詞相符的代名詞必須是反身代名詞——但反身代名詞只適合放在子句結尾或緊接在主詞後面，絕不會出現在像 "diagnosis" 這樣的名詞之前。
part5.tipFr: "Himself" est le choix erroné le plus courant ici car les apprenants supposent que tout pronom correspondant au sujet doit être réfléchi — mais un pronom réfléchi ne convient qu'en fin de proposition ou juste après le sujet, jamais juste avant un nom comme "diagnosis".
part5.tipKo: "Himself"는 여기서 가장 흔한 오답인데, 학습자들이 주어와 일치하는 대명사는 재귀대명사여야 한다고 가정하기 때문입니다 — 하지만 재귀대명사는 절의 끝이나 주어 바로 뒤에만 어울리며, "diagnosis" 같은 명사 바로 앞에는 결코 오지 않습니다.
part5.tipJa: "Himself" はここで最もよくある間違った選択です。学習者は主語に一致する代名詞は再帰代名詞でなければならないと思い込みがちだからです — しかし再帰代名詞は節の終わりか主語の直後にしか合わず、"diagnosis" のような名詞の直前には決して来ません。
part5.tipId: "Himself" adalah pilihan salah yang paling umum di sini karena pelajar mengasumsikan bahwa kata ganti apa pun yang cocok dengan subjek harus bersifat refleksif — tetapi kata ganti refleksif hanya cocok di akhir klausa atau tepat setelah subjek, tidak pernah tepat sebelum kata benda seperti "diagnosis".
part5.tipEl: Το "himself" είναι η πιο συνηθισμένη λανθασμένη επιλογή εδώ επειδή οι μαθητές υποθέτουν ότι κάθε αντωνυμία που ταιριάζει με το υποκείμενο πρέπει να είναι αναφορική — αλλά μια αναφορική αντωνυμία ταιριάζει μόνο στο τέλος μιας πρότασης ή αμέσως μετά το υποκείμενο, ποτέ ακριβώς πριν από ένα ουσιαστικό όπως το "diagnosis".
part5.tipEs: "Himself" es la elección incorrecta más común aquí porque los estudiantes asumen que cualquier pronombre que coincida con el sujeto debe ser reflexivo — pero un pronombre reflexivo solo encaja al final de una cláusula o justo después del sujeto, nunca justo antes de un sustantivo como "diagnosis".

part5.tip: "Later" is an easy wrong pick since it relates to time like "recent" does, but "the most recent" is the fixed collocation for describing something newest — "the most later" is never grammatical, so collocation, not just meaning, rules this one out.
part5.tipVn: "Later" là lựa chọn sai dễ mắc vì nó liên quan đến thời gian giống "recent", nhưng "the most recent" là collocation cố định để mô tả điều mới nhất — "the most later" không bao giờ đúng ngữ pháp, nên chính collocation (chứ không chỉ nghĩa) loại trừ đáp án này.
part5.tipTh: "Later" เป็นตัวเลือกผิดที่เลือกง่ายเพราะเกี่ยวข้องกับเวลาเหมือน "recent" แต่ "the most recent" เป็น collocation ตายตัวสำหรับอธิบายสิ่งที่ใหม่ที่สุด — "the most later" ไม่เคยถูกไวยากรณ์ ดังนั้น collocation ไม่ใช่แค่ความหมาย คือสิ่งที่ตัดตัวเลือกนี้ออก
part5.tipZh: "Later" 是容易誤選的答案，因為它和 "recent" 一樣與時間有關，但 "the most recent" 是描述最新事物的固定搭配——"the most later" 在文法上永遠不成立，所以是搭配本身（而不僅是語意）排除了這個選項。
part5.tipFr: "Later" est un choix erroné facile puisqu'il est lié au temps comme "recent", mais "the most recent" est la collocation fixe pour décrire quelque chose de plus récent — "the most later" n'est jamais grammatical, donc c'est la collocation, pas seulement le sens, qui l'exclut.
part5.tipKo: "Later"는 "recent"처럼 시간과 관련이 있어 고르기 쉬운 오답이지만, "the most recent"는 가장 최신의 것을 묘사하는 고정 연어입니다 — "the most later"는 결코 문법적으로 성립하지 않으므로, 의미뿐 아니라 연어 자체가 이 답을 배제합니다.
part5.tipJa: "Later" は "recent" と同様に時間に関連するため選びやすい誤答ですが、"the most recent" は最新のものを表す固定コロケーションです — "the most later" は決して文法的に成立しないため、意味だけでなくコロケーション自体がこれを除外します。
part5.tipId: "Later" adalah pilihan salah yang mudah karena berkaitan dengan waktu seperti "recent", tetapi "the most recent" adalah kolokasi tetap untuk menggambarkan sesuatu yang terbaru — "the most later" tidak pernah gramatikal, jadi kolokasilah, bukan hanya makna, yang menyingkirkan pilihan ini.
part5.tipEl: Το "later" είναι μια εύκολη λανθασμένη επιλογή αφού σχετίζεται με τον χρόνο όπως το "recent", αλλά το "the most recent" είναι η σταθερή συνάφεια για να περιγράψει κάτι πιο πρόσφατο — το "the most later" δεν είναι ποτέ γραμματικά σωστό, οπότε η συνάφεια, όχι μόνο η σημασία, αποκλείει αυτή την επιλογή.
part5.tipEs: "Later" es una elección incorrecta fácil ya que se relaciona con el tiempo como "recent", pero "the most recent" es la colocación fija para describir algo más nuevo — "the most later" nunca es gramatical, así que es la colocación, no solo el significado, lo que descarta esta opción.

part5.tip: "Remarkably" is tempting because it's also an adverb of degree, but it means "notably" (drawing attention), not "rigidly/exactly" — read for the precise shade of meaning the legal context needs (strict adherence to evidence), not just the right part of speech.
part5.tipVn: "Remarkably" hấp dẫn vì cũng là trạng từ chỉ mức độ, nhưng nó nghĩa là "đáng chú ý", không phải "nghiêm ngặt/chính xác" — hãy đọc kỹ sắc thái nghĩa mà ngữ cảnh pháp lý cần (tuân thủ chặt chẽ bằng chứng), không chỉ đúng từ loại.
part5.tipTh: "Remarkably" น่าดึงดูดเพราะเป็นกริยาวิเศษณ์บอกระดับด้วย แต่หมายถึง "น่าสังเกต" (ดึงดูดความสนใจ) ไม่ใช่ "เข้มงวด/แม่นยำ" — อ่านเพื่อหาความหมายที่แม่นยำที่บริบทกฎหมายต้องการ (การยึดมั่นในหลักฐานอย่างเคร่งครัด) ไม่ใช่แค่ชนิดของคำที่ถูกต้อง
part5.tipZh: "Remarkably" 很誘人，因為它也是程度副詞，但它的意思是「引人注目地」，而非「嚴格地／精確地」——請閱讀法律語境所需的精確語意（嚴格遵循證據），而不僅是詞性正確與否。
part5.tipFr: "Remarkably" est tentant car c'est aussi un adverbe de degré, mais il signifie "notablement" (attirer l'attention), pas "rigoureusement/exactement" — cherchez la nuance précise de sens dont le contexte juridique a besoin (adhésion stricte aux preuves), pas seulement la bonne nature grammaticale.
part5.tipKo: "Remarkably"도 정도를 나타내는 부사이기 때문에 유혹적이지만, 이는 "엄격하게/정확하게"가 아니라 "눈에 띄게"(주목을 끄는)라는 뜻입니다 — 올바른 품사만이 아니라, 법적 맥락(증거에 대한 엄격한 준수)이 필요로 하는 정확한 의미 뉘앙스를 읽어야 합니다.
part5.tipJa: "Remarkably" も程度を表す副詞なので魅力的ですが、意味は「厳格に／正確に」ではなく「著しく」（注目を集める）です — 品詞が正しいだけでなく、法的文脈が必要とする正確な意味合い（証拠への厳格な準拠）を読み取りましょう。
part5.tipId: "Remarkably" menggoda karena juga merupakan kata keterangan tingkatan, tetapi artinya "secara mencolok" (menarik perhatian), bukan "secara ketat/tepat" — baca nuansa makna yang tepat yang dibutuhkan konteks hukum (kepatuhan ketat pada bukti), bukan hanya jenis kata yang benar.
part5.tipEl: Το "remarkably" είναι δελεαστικό επειδή είναι επίσης επίρρημα βαθμού, αλλά σημαίνει "αξιοσημείωτα" (τραβώντας την προσοχή), όχι "αυστηρά/ακριβώς" — διαβάστε για την ακριβή απόχρωση σημασίας που χρειάζεται το νομικό πλαίσιο (αυστηρή προσήλωση στα στοιχεία), όχι μόνο το σωστό μέρος του λόγου.
part5.tipEs: "Remarkably" es tentador porque también es un adverbio de grado, pero significa "notablemente" (llamar la atención), no "rigurosamente/exactamente" — busca el matiz preciso de significado que necesita el contexto legal (apego estricto a la evidencia), no solo la categoría gramatical correcta.

part5.tipTh: เมื่อช่องว่างอยู่ทันทีหลัง "the" ผู้เข้าสอบบางครั้งเลือกตัวเลือกที่ดูเหมือนคำคุณศัพท์แทนคำนาม — จำคำลงท้ายคำนามทั่วไป (-or, -er, -ant, -ee) เพื่อให้จำได้ทันทีว่า "instructors" เป็นคำนามที่ประโยคต้องการ

part5.tipKo: 빈칸이 "the" 바로 뒤에 있을 때, 응시자들은 때때로 명사 대신 형용사처럼 보이는 선택지를 고릅니다 — 흔한 명사 어미(-or, -er, -ant, -ee)를 외워두면 "instructors"가 문장에 필요한 명사임을 즉시 알아챌 수 있습니다.

part5.tip: A personal pronoun like "them" looks like an easy fit at the end of a sentence, but right after a noun ("the vehicles") referring back to that same noun, only the reflexive form "themselves" is grammatically correct.
part5.tipVn: Đại từ nhân xưng như "them" trông có vẻ dễ khớp ở cuối câu, nhưng ngay sau một danh từ ("the vehicles") chỉ lại chính danh từ đó, chỉ có dạng phản thân "themselves" mới đúng ngữ pháp.
part5.tipTh: สรรพนามบุคคลอย่าง "them" ดูเหมือนจะเข้ากันได้ง่ายที่ท้ายประโยค แต่ทันทีหลังคำนาม ("the vehicles") ที่อ้างอิงกลับไปยังคำนามเดียวกันนั้น มีเพียงรูปสะท้อน "themselves" เท่านั้นที่ถูกต้องตามไวยากรณ์
part5.tipZh: 像 "them" 這樣的人稱代名詞看似很容易放在句尾，但緊接在指回同一名詞的名詞（"the vehicles"）之後，只有反身形式 "themselves" 才符合文法。
part5.tipFr: Un pronom personnel comme "them" semble facile à placer en fin de phrase, mais juste après un nom ("the vehicles") qui réfère à ce même nom, seule la forme réfléchie "themselves" est grammaticalement correcte.
part5.tipKo: "them" 같은 인칭대명사는 문장 끝에 쉽게 맞는 것처럼 보이지만, 같은 명사를 다시 가리키는 명사("the vehicles") 바로 뒤에서는 재귀형인 "themselves"만이 문법적으로 옳습니다.
part5.tipJa: "them" のような人称代名詞は文末に簡単に収まりそうに見えますが、同じ名詞を指し戻す名詞（"the vehicles"）の直後では、再帰形の "themselves" だけが文法的に正しいです。
part5.tipId: Kata ganti orang seperti "them" terlihat mudah cocok di akhir kalimat, tetapi tepat setelah kata benda ("the vehicles") yang merujuk kembali ke kata benda yang sama itu, hanya bentuk refleksif "themselves" yang benar secara gramatikal.

part5.tip: "Function" and "distance" are both abstract nouns that could plausibly follow "in the southern ___", but only "region" pairs naturally with a geographic direction — test whether the noun can physically be located on a map.
part5.tipVn: "Function" và "distance" đều là danh từ trừu tượng có thể hợp lý đứng sau "in the southern ___", nhưng chỉ "region" mới kết hợp tự nhiên với hướng địa lý — hãy kiểm tra xem danh từ đó có thể định vị được trên bản đồ hay không.
part5.tipTh: "Function" และ "distance" ต่างก็เป็นคำนามนามธรรมที่อาจตามหลัง "in the southern ___" ได้อย่างสมเหตุสมผล แต่มีเพียง "region" เท่านั้นที่จับคู่กับทิศทางภูมิศาสตร์ได้อย่างเป็นธรรมชาติ — ทดสอบว่าคำนามนั้นสามารถระบุตำแหน่งบนแผนที่ได้จริงหรือไม่

part5.tipFr: "Function" et "distance" sont tous deux des noms abstraits qui pourraient plausiblement suivre "in the southern ___", mais seul "region" s'associe naturellement à une direction géographique — testez si le nom peut être physiquement situé sur une carte.

part5.tipId: "Function" dan "distance" sama-sama kata benda abstrak yang bisa masuk akal mengikuti "in the southern ___", tetapi hanya "region" yang berpasangan secara alami dengan arah geografis — uji apakah kata benda itu bisa secara fisik berada di peta.

part5.tipId: Setelah bentuk posesif ("its"), peserta tes terkadang salah memilih bentuk kata kerja — hanya kata benda seperti "creation" yang bisa mengikuti kata ganti posesif, jadi latih diri Anda untuk selalu mengharapkan kata benda tepat setelah "its/his/her/their".

part5.tipZh: "Presentation" 和 "presenting" 聽起來都是這個概念合理的名詞化形式，但兩者在 "is" 後面描述房屋狀態時都說不通——"presentable"（形容詞，意為整潔/吸引人）是唯一在文法和語意上都合適的選項。
part5.tipFr: "Presentation" et "presenting" sonnent tous deux comme des nominalisations raisonnables de l'idée, mais aucun n'a de sens après "is" décrivant l'état d'une maison — "presentable" (adjectif signifiant net/attrayant) est la seule option qui convient à la fois grammaticalement et sémantiquement.
part5.tipKo: "Presentation"과 "presenting" 둘 다 그 개념의 그럴듯한 명사화처럼 들리지만, 집의 상태를 설명하는 "is" 뒤에서는 둘 다 의미가 통하지 않습니다 — "presentable"(단정한/매력적인이라는 뜻의 형용사)만이 문법과 의미 모두에 맞는 유일한 선택지입니다.
part5.tipJa: "Presentation" と "presenting" はどちらもその概念の妥当な名詞化のように聞こえますが、家の状態を説明する "is" の後ではどちらも意味が通じません — "presentable"（きちんとした・魅力的という意味の形容詞）が文法的にも意味的にも合う唯一の選択肢です。
part5.tipId: "Presentation" dan "presenting" sama-sama terdengar seperti nominalisasi yang masuk akal dari gagasan itu, tetapi keduanya tidak masuk akal setelah "is" yang menggambarkan keadaan sebuah rumah — "presentable" (kata sifat berarti rapi/menarik) adalah satu-satunya pilihan yang cocok baik secara tata bahasa maupun makna.
part5.tipEl: Τόσο το "presentation" όσο και το "presenting" ακούγονται σαν λογικές ονοματοποιήσεις της ιδέας, αλλά κανένα δεν βγάζει νόημα μετά το "is" που περιγράφει την κατάσταση ενός σπιτιού — το "presentable" (επίθετο που σημαίνει καθαρό/ελκυστικό) είναι η μόνη επιλογή που ταιριάζει τόσο γραμματικά όσο και νοηματικά.
part5.tipEs: "Presentation" y "presenting" suenan ambos como nominalizaciones razonables de la idea, pero ninguno tiene sentido después de "is" describiendo el estado de una casa — "presentable" (adjetivo que significa ordenado/atractivo) es la única opción que encaja tanto gramatical como semánticamente.

part5.tip: This is a reduced relative clause ("the payment [which was] remitted last week") — learners often miss that the missing "which was" means the blank needs a past participle like "remitted", not a base verb or noun.
part5.tipVn: Đây là mệnh đề quan hệ rút gọn ("the payment [which was] remitted last week") — người học thường bỏ sót rằng phần "which was" bị lược bỏ có nghĩa chỗ trống cần một quá khứ phân từ như "remitted", không phải động từ nguyên mẫu hay danh từ.
part5.tipTh: นี่คืออนุประโยคขยายความแบบรูปย่อ ("the payment [which was] remitted last week") — ผู้เรียนมักพลาดว่า "which was" ที่หายไปหมายความว่าช่องว่างต้องการ past participle อย่าง "remitted" ไม่ใช่กริยาเดิมหรือคำนาม
part5.tipZh: 這是一個省略的關係子句（"the payment [which was] remitted last week"）——學習者常常忽略了消失的 "which was" 意味著空格需要過去分詞如 "remitted"，而不是原形動詞或名詞。
part5.tipFr: Il s'agit d'une proposition relative réduite ("the payment [which was] remitted last week") — les apprenants oublient souvent que le "which was" manquant signifie que l'espace nécessite un participe passé comme "remitted", pas un verbe de base ou un nom.
part5.tipKo: 이것은 축약된 관계절입니다("the payment [which was] remitted last week") — 학습자들은 종종 생략된 "which was"가 빈칸에 동사 원형이나 명사가 아니라 "remitted" 같은 과거분사가 필요함을 의미한다는 것을 놓칩니다.
part5.tipJa: これは縮約された関係詞節です（"the payment [which was] remitted last week"）— 学習者は、省略された "which was" が、空欄に動詞の原形や名詞ではなく "remitted" のような過去分詞が必要であることを意味していることをよく見逃します。
part5.tipId: Ini adalah klausa relatif yang diperpendek ("the payment [which was] remitted last week") — pelajar sering melewatkan bahwa "which was" yang hilang berarti bagian kosong membutuhkan past participle seperti "remitted", bukan kata kerja dasar atau kata benda.
part5.tipEl: Αυτή είναι μια συνεσταλμένη αναφορική πρόταση ("the payment [which was] remitted last week") — οι μαθητές συχνά παραβλέπουν ότι το ελλείπον "which was" σημαίνει ότι το κενό χρειάζεται μετοχή παρελθόντα χρόνου όπως το "remitted", όχι βασικό ρήμα ή ουσιαστικό.
part5.tipEs: Esta es una cláusula relativa reducida ("the payment [which was] remitted last week") — los estudiantes a menudo pasan por alto que el "which was" faltante significa que el espacio necesita un participio pasado como "remitted", no un verbo base ni un sustantivo.

part5.tip: "Because" is tempting since the sentence involves a condition-like delay, but "because" signals a reason/cause, while "until" signals a time boundary ("up to the time that") — the sentence is about waiting for approval, not explaining why.
part5.tipVn: "Because" hấp dẫn vì câu có vẻ liên quan đến một sự trì hoãn giống điều kiện, nhưng "because" báo hiệu lý do/nguyên nhân, còn "until" báo hiệu ranh giới thời gian ("cho đến khi") — câu này nói về việc chờ phê duyệt, không phải giải thích lý do.
part5.tipTh: "Because" น่าดึงดูดเพราะประโยคเกี่ยวข้องกับความล่าช้าคล้ายเงื่อนไข แต่ "because" ส่งสัญญาณเหตุผล/สาเหตุ ในขณะที่ "until" ส่งสัญญาณขอบเขตเวลา ("จนกว่าจะถึงเวลาที่") — ประโยคนี้เกี่ยวกับการรอการอนุมัติ ไม่ใช่การอธิบายเหตุผล
part5.tipZh: "Because" 很誘人，因為句子涉及類似條件的延遲，但 "because" 表示原因/理由，而 "until" 表示時間界限（「直到……為止」）——這句話講的是等待批准，而不是解釋原因。
part5.tipFr: "Because" est tentant car la phrase implique un retard de type conditionnel, mais "because" signale une raison/cause, tandis que "until" signale une limite temporelle ("jusqu'au moment où") — la phrase parle d'attendre une approbation, pas d'expliquer pourquoi.
part5.tipKo: 문장이 조건 같은 지연을 포함하기 때문에 "Because"는 유혹적이지만, "because"는 이유/원인을 나타내고 "until"은 시간적 경계("~할 때까지")를 나타냅니다 — 이 문장은 이유를 설명하는 것이 아니라 승인을 기다리는 것에 관한 것입니다.
part5.tipJa: 文が条件のような遅延を含んでいるため "Because" は魅力的ですが、"because" は理由・原因を示し、"until" は時間的な境界（「〜する時まで」）を示します — この文は理由を説明しているのではなく、承認を待つことについてです。
part5.tipId: "Because" menggoda karena kalimat melibatkan penundaan yang mirip kondisi, tetapi "because" menandakan alasan/sebab, sedangkan "until" menandakan batas waktu ("sampai waktu ketika") — kalimat ini tentang menunggu persetujuan, bukan menjelaskan alasan.
part5.tipEl: Το "because" είναι δελεαστικό αφού η πρόταση αφορά μια καθυστέρηση σαν συνθήκη, αλλά το "because" σηματοδοτεί έναν λόγο/αιτία, ενώ το "until" σηματοδοτεί ένα χρονικό όριο ("μέχρι τη στιγμή που") — η πρόταση αφορά την αναμονή έγκρισης, όχι την εξήγηση του γιατί.
part5.tipEs: "Because" es tentador ya que la oración implica un retraso similar a una condición, pero "because" señala una razón/causa, mientras que "until" señala un límite temporal ("hasta el momento en que") — la oración trata sobre esperar una aprobación, no sobre explicar por qué.

part5.tipKo: "Value"도 긍정적인 추상명사이기 때문에 까다로운 오답이지만, 문장은 "가치/중요성"이 아니라 "무언가를 하려는 노력"(attempt)을 의미하는 명사가 필요합니다 — 선택한 단어를 항상 문장에 다시 넣어서 의미가 진짜로 맞는지 확인하세요.
part5.tipJa: "Value" もポジティブな抽象名詞であるため紛らわしい誤答ですが、文が必要としているのは「価値・重要性」ではなく「何かをしようとする努力」（attempt）を意味する名詞です — 選んだ語を必ず文に戻して、意味が本当に合っているかテストしましょう。
part5.tipId: "Value" adalah jebakan yang sulit dibedakan karena juga merupakan kata benda abstrak positif, tetapi kalimat membutuhkan kata benda yang berarti "upaya untuk melakukan sesuatu" (attempt), bukan "nilai/kepentingan" — selalu substitusikan kembali kata yang Anda pilih ke dalam kalimat untuk menguji apakah maknanya benar-benar cocok.
part5.tipEl: Το "value" είναι μια δύσκολη σχεδόν σωστή επιλογή επειδή είναι επίσης θετικό αφηρημένο ουσιαστικό, αλλά η πρόταση χρειάζεται ουσιαστικό που σημαίνει "μια προσπάθεια να κάνεις κάτι" (attempt), όχι "αξία/σημασία" — αντικαταστήστε πάντα τη λέξη που επιλέξατε πίσω στην πρόταση για να ελέγξετε αν το νόημα ταιριάζει πραγματικά.
part5.tipEs: "Value" es una casi-coincidencia complicada porque también es un sustantivo abstracto positivo, pero la oración necesita un sustantivo que signifique "un esfuerzo por hacer algo" (attempt), no "valor/importancia" — siempre sustituye la palabra elegida de nuevo en la oración para probar si el significado realmente encaja.

part5.tipZh: 當句子讀起來即使沒有空格也文法完整時，缺少的詞很可能是副詞——不要因為句子主題（安全/事故）讓人覺得需要一個「更重的」詞，就過度思考變成名詞或形容詞。
part5.tipFr: Quand une phrase se lit comme grammaticalement complète sans l'espace, le mot manquant est probablement un adverbe — ne le sur-analysez pas en un nom ou un adjectif juste parce que le sujet de la phrase (sécurité/accidents) donne l'impression d'avoir besoin d'un mot "plus lourd".
part5.tipKo: 빈칸 없이도 문장이 문법적으로 완전하게 읽힌다면, 빠진 단어는 부사일 가능성이 높습니다 — 문장 주제(안전/사고)가 "더 무거운" 단어가 필요하다고 느끼게 한다고 해서 명사나 형용사로 지나치게 생각하지 마세요.
part5.tipJa: 空欄がなくても文が文法的に完成しているように読める場合、欠けている語はおそらく副詞です — 文の話題（安全・事故）が「より重い」語を必要とするように感じさせるからといって、名詞や形容詞だと考えすぎないようにしましょう。
part5.tipId: Ketika kalimat terbaca lengkap secara gramatikal tanpa bagian kosong, kata yang hilang kemungkinan besar adalah kata keterangan — jangan terlalu memikirkannya menjadi kata benda atau kata sifat hanya karena topik kalimat (keselamatan/kecelakaan) terasa membutuhkan kata yang "lebih berat".
part5.tipEl: Όταν μια πρόταση διαβάζεται ως γραμματικά πλήρης χωρίς το κενό, η λέξη που λείπει είναι πιθανότατα επίρρημα — μην το υπερ-αναλύετε σε ουσιαστικό ή επίθετο απλώς επειδή το θέμα της πρότασης (ασφάλεια/ατυχήματα) δίνει την αίσθηση ότι χρειάζεται μια "βαρύτερη" λέξη.
part5.tipEs: Cuando una oración se lee como gramaticalmente completa sin el espacio, la palabra faltante probablemente sea un adverbio — no lo sobreanalices convirtiéndolo en sustantivo o adjetivo solo porque el tema de la oración (seguridad/accidentes) da la sensación de necesitar una palabra "más pesada".

part5.tip: "Substantially" is a common wrong pick because it also implies a significant degree, but it means "to a great extent", the opposite frequency implication of "occasionally" (from time to time) that the sentence about allowing rehearsal viewing needs.
part5.tipVn: "Substantially" là lựa chọn sai phổ biến vì cũng ngụ ý mức độ đáng kể, nhưng nó nghĩa "ở mức độ lớn", ngược với hàm ý tần suất của "occasionally" (thỉnh thoảng) mà câu về việc cho phép xem buổi tập cần đến.
part5.tipTh: "Substantially" เป็นตัวเลือกผิดที่พบบ่อยเพราะยังบ่งบอกถึงระดับที่สำคัญด้วย แต่หมายถึง "ในระดับมาก" ซึ่งเป็นความหมายความถี่ตรงข้ามกับ "occasionally" (เป็นครั้งคราว) ที่ประโยคเกี่ยวกับการอนุญาตให้ดูการซ้อมต้องการ
part5.tipZh: "Substantially" 是常見的錯誤選項，因為它也暗示相當大的程度，但它意思是「在很大程度上」，與句子中關於允許觀看排練所需的 "occasionally"（偶爾）在頻率上恰恰相反。
part5.tipFr: "Substantially" est un choix erroné courant car il implique aussi un degré significatif, mais il signifie "dans une large mesure", l'implication de fréquence opposée à "occasionally" (de temps en temps) dont a besoin la phrase sur l'autorisation de voir les répétitions.
part5.tipKo: "Substantially"도 상당한 정도를 암시하기 때문에 흔한 오답이지만, 이는 "상당한 정도로"라는 뜻으로, 리허설 관람을 허용하는 것에 관한 문장이 필요로 하는 "occasionally"(가끔)의 빈도 의미와는 반대입니다.
part5.tipJa: "Substantially" もかなりの程度を示唆するためよくある誤答ですが、これは「大きな程度で」という意味であり、リハーサル鑑賞の許可についての文が必要とする "occasionally"（時々）の頻度の含意とは正反対です。
part5.tipId: "Substantially" adalah pilihan salah yang umum karena juga menyiratkan tingkat yang signifikan, tetapi artinya "pada tingkat yang besar", implikasi frekuensi yang berlawanan dengan "occasionally" (sesekali) yang dibutuhkan kalimat tentang mengizinkan menonton latihan.
part5.tipEl: Το "substantially" είναι μια συχνή λανθασμένη επιλογή επειδή υπονοεί επίσης σημαντικό βαθμό, αλλά σημαίνει "σε μεγάλο βαθμό", την αντίθετη υπόνοια συχνότητας από το "occasionally" (κατά καιρούς) που χρειάζεται η πρόταση για την άδεια παρακολούθησης προβών.
part5.tipEs: "Substantially" es una elección incorrecta común porque también implica un grado significativo, pero significa "en gran medida", la implicación de frecuencia opuesta a "occasionally" (de vez en cuando) que necesita la oración sobre permitir ver los ensayos.

part5.tip: "So" is a tempting wrong pick because it can also connect two related ideas, but it means "therefore" (a result), while "with" here means "by means of" — check whether the second half of the sentence explains a cause/result or a method.
part5.tipVn: "So" là lựa chọn sai hấp dẫn vì cũng có thể nối hai ý liên quan, nhưng nó nghĩa "vì vậy" (kết quả), trong khi "with" ở đây nghĩa "bằng cách" — hãy kiểm tra xem nửa sau của câu đang giải thích nguyên nhân/kết quả hay một phương pháp.
part5.tipTh: "So" เป็นตัวเลือกผิดที่น่าดึงดูดเพราะสามารถเชื่อมสองแนวคิดที่เกี่ยวข้องกันได้ด้วย แต่หมายถึง "ดังนั้น" (ผลลัพธ์) ในขณะที่ "with" ที่นี่หมายถึง "โดยวิธีการ" — ตรวจสอบว่าครึ่งหลังของประโยคอธิบายเหตุ/ผลหรือวิธีการ
part5.tipZh: "So" 是誘人的錯誤選項，因為它也可以連接兩個相關的概念，但它的意思是「因此」（結果），而這裡的 "with" 意思是「透過……方式」——請檢查句子的後半部分是在解釋因果還是方法。
part5.tipFr: "So" est un choix erroné tentant car il peut aussi relier deux idées liées, mais il signifie "donc" (un résultat), tandis que "with" ici signifie "au moyen de" — vérifiez si la seconde moitié de la phrase explique une cause/résultat ou une méthode.
part5.tipKo: "So"는 두 관련 개념을 연결할 수도 있어 유혹적인 오답이지만, 이는 "그러므로"(결과)라는 뜻이고 여기서 "with"는 "~을 통해"라는 뜻입니다 — 문장의 뒷부분이 원인/결과를 설명하는지 방법을 설명하는지 확인하세요.
part5.tipJa: "So" は二つの関連した考えをつなげることもできるため魅力的な誤答ですが、これは「したがって」（結果）を意味し、ここでの "with" は「〜によって」を意味します — 文の後半が原因・結果を説明しているのか、方法を説明しているのかを確認しましょう。
part5.tipId: "So" adalah pilihan salah yang menggoda karena juga bisa menghubungkan dua gagasan yang berkaitan, tetapi artinya "oleh karena itu" (suatu hasil), sedangkan "with" di sini berarti "dengan cara" — periksa apakah bagian kedua kalimat menjelaskan sebab/akibat atau suatu metode.
part5.tipEl: Το "so" είναι μια δελεαστική λανθασμένη επιλογή επειδή μπορεί επίσης να συνδέει δύο σχετικές ιδέες, αλλά σημαίνει "επομένως" (ένα αποτέλεσμα), ενώ το "with" εδώ σημαίνει "με το μέσο" — ελέγξτε αν το δεύτερο μισό της πρότασης εξηγεί αιτία/αποτέλεσμα ή μια μέθοδο.
part5.tipEs: "So" es una elección incorrecta tentadora porque también puede conectar dos ideas relacionadas, pero significa "por lo tanto" (un resultado), mientras que "with" aquí significa "por medio de" — verifica si la segunda mitad de la oración explica una causa/resultado o un método.

part5.tip: "As long as" is a strong distractor because it also expresses a time/condition relationship, but it must be followed by a full clause, while the blank here is followed by a noun phrase ("the candidate's official announcement") — check the grammar of what follows before the meaning.
part5.tipVn: "As long as" là bẫy mạnh vì cũng diễn tả quan hệ thời gian/điều kiện, nhưng nó phải theo sau bởi một mệnh đề đầy đủ, trong khi chỗ trống ở đây theo sau là một cụm danh từ ("the candidate's official announcement") — hãy kiểm tra ngữ pháp của phần theo sau trước khi xét đến nghĩa.
part5.tipTh: "As long as" เป็นตัวลวงที่แข็งแกร่งเพราะยังแสดงความสัมพันธ์เวลา/เงื่อนไขด้วย แต่ต้องตามด้วยอนุประโยคเต็ม ในขณะที่ช่องว่างที่นี่ตามด้วยวลีคำนาม ("the candidate's official announcement") — ตรวจสอบไวยากรณ์ของสิ่งที่ตามมาก่อนความหมาย
part5.tipZh: "As long as" 是強有力的干擾項，因為它也表達時間/條件關係，但它後面必須接完整子句，而這裡的空格後面接的是名詞片語（"the candidate's official announcement"）——請先檢查後面內容的文法，再考慮語意。

part5.tipKo: "As long as"도 시간/조건 관계를 나타내기 때문에 강력한 오답이지만, 반드시 완전한 절이 뒤따라야 하는 반면, 여기 빈칸 뒤에는 명사구("the candidate's official announcement")가 옵니다 — 의미보다 먼저 뒤따르는 내용의 문법을 확인하세요.
part5.tipJa: "As long as" も時間・条件の関係を表すため強力な誤答ですが、後には完全な節が続かなければならず、ここでの空欄の後には名詞句（"the candidate's official announcement"）が続きます — 意味の前に、後に続くものの文法を確認しましょう。

part7.description:
It's Raining Cats and Dogs

Brentwood (May 2) - - [1] - Brentwood City finally has its very own cat cafe called Catastrophe and dog cafe called Hotdogs, both opened by owners Kevin and Ginger Blake. Both cafes opened last month to fanfare and a great deal of press coverage. - [2] - "Business has been booming", says Kevin Blake. "We knew we'd be successful; we just didn't think we'd be this successfull". Not only are customers enthusiastically flocking to both cafes to hang out with the animals while drinking coffee and tea, many of them are adopting the animals and giving them forever homes. - [3] - "We thought it would be a good idea to take in some of the animals because of the overcrowding in many of the shelters", explained Ginger Blake. "And customers have a chance to interact with the animals, which is the best form of advertisement for the shelters." Since the cafes' opening, more than 10 dogs and 15 cats have been adopted. "I don't yet own a dog, but I've always wanted one," says Laurie Jordan, a regular customer. "I come here to play with them. Maybe one day I'll find a dog that I really want." - [4] -
Because of the success, the Blakes are considering expanding by purchasing the adjacent shops. "We need more space to fit all our customers and the animals," explained Kevin. "It can get very crowded at times," The Blakes are looking to renovate the dog cafe next month and the cat cafe during the fall.

Hello, I'd like to get an update on the progress of the drapes that the Manilloa Family ordered.

Lucy Mitt (9:41)
We're still waiting for the lace silks from Hand-Made Lace but we received most of the other fabrics yesterday. Our seamstresses will get to work on those today.

Bill Flake (9:42)
Then do you think the project will be completed by this Friday as the Manillao's wanted?

Lucy Mitt (9:43)

Lucy Mitt (9:45)
Actually, Richard is taking care of that. Any word from them, Richard?

Yes, I just got off the phone with them. There was a bit of a delay because the lace artisans used the wrong silks. They had to re-work the lace. We'll receive them this afternoon. They sent a rush delivery to us.

Bill Flake (9:46)
Excellent. Then can the drapes be finished at the end of this week?

Lucy Mitt (9:47)
No problem. We'll work around the clock to get them finished on time.

5th Annual Summer Fun Festival
Sunday, July 23

10:00 A.M. to 6:00 P.M. Local Nature Art Competition
Duluth artists will be displaying their paintings of local nature and wildlife in the Duluth Community Center. Visitors are asked to cast their vote for their favorite painting. The winner will be announced at the start of the singing competition.

11:00 A.M. to 12:00 P.M. Magic Show
Please join us for an astonishing magic show. Magician Mick Turner is famous for his creative and entertaining magic tricks.

12:00 P.M. to 2:00 P.M. Live Jazz Concert
Enjoy live jazz in the park performed by New-York-based jazz band The Holioway Band. They will be playing a variety of jazz standards. They will also have their most recent record for sale.

10:00 A.M. to 7:00 P.M. Renewable Energy Expo
Local company Sunshine Energy will be displaying some of its newest renewable energy projects, including solar panels and portable cell phone chargers.

7:00 P.M. to 9:00 P.M. Singing Competition
Local residents are encouraged to take part in this year's singing competition. Those who would like to participate can register by visiting our website at www.duluthGitysff.com and filling out the necessary form.

For more information, please call us at 555-0157.

part7.description:
Movies in the Park

This fall Glenwood Springs Park will host a weekly Movies in the Park night for residents of Gilenwood Springs. In cooperation with various local business sponsors including Paxton Inc. and GS Mall, family-friendly movies will be shown every Friday night at the center of the park. Tickets are not necessary for these events because they are free to the public.

Running from September through November, Movies in the Park promises a wonderful line-up of fun and touching movies for the whole family. You are encouraged to bring blankets and chairs as well as picnic snacks. Movie starting times depend on sunset times, so it is advised to come early to secure your spot beforehand. Please visit our website at www..gllenwoodsprings.org/movies to see a schedule of upcoming films and a list of our local sponsors.

In the event of heavy rain, low temperatures, or strong winds, the film screening may be canceled. If this occurs, the announcement for the film cancellation will be made both on our website and on the local radio. You can also ask about event cancellations by calling the Glenwood Springs Department of Parks and Recreation at 715-555-5358.

part7.description:
Kenneth Global Journalism internship

The Kenneth Global Journalism Internship will provide you with great opportunities to train with the world's most renowned international multimedia news agency, work with professional reporters and editors, and gain valuable experiences in fast-paced newsrooms in big cities such as London, Berlin, and Paris. It will offer talented college graduates an opportunity to learn and develop their journalistic skills and first-hand knowledge.

This is a paid internship that offers free lodging as well as lunch and dinner. Interns will receive several weeks of formal training focused on writing skills, journalism ethics, and basic workplace knowledge. They are also able to take advantage of other regularly scheduled training opportunities during the internship free of charge. The internship will last 4 months, beginning on August 1.

Applications for the internship can be found on our website at www.kennethglobal.com and must be submitted by June 20. Applicants who advance past this stage will be asked to interview at our headquarters on June 27. Any questions can be directed toward Ruby Hart at rubyhart@kennethglobal.com or asked in person at our headquarters in Austin.
From: Kyle Lane <kylelane12@mpnet.com>
To: Ruby Hart <rubyhart@kennethglobal.com>
Subject: Internship
Date: June 28
Dear Ms. Hart,

I am extremely grateful to have advanced past the first round of the Kenneth Global Journalism Internship's selection process. Applicants are supposed to interview in person on the specified date, but unfortunately I am scheduled to attend an important conference in Dallas with my professor. However, because I live in the same city as your headquarters, it would not be difficult to arrange an alternative time for me to interview.

Thanks again for considering me for this position. I look forward to hearing back from you concerning a possible interview date. In the meantime, I will do my best to prepare myself.

Regards,
Kyle Lane

part7.description:
To: Sam Berry <sberry@princetheater.com>
From: Bessie Wagner <bessiewagner@linsuniversity.edu>
Date: July 4
Subject: Openings
Dear Mr. Berry,

My name is Bessie Wagner and Iam currently a student in the theater department at Lins University. I have almost finished my degree, and I am starting to look into possible career opportunities for my future. A professor of mine recommended that I contact you at the Prince Theater to ask about possible positions at your company.

At Lins University, I specialized in the production elements of theater. Through both academic and practical experiences, I learned the useful skills necessary for stage management. As of September, I will be available to work either part-time or full-time and apply myself fully to whatever task is assigned to me.

I would really appreciate it if you let me know if there are any available positions starting this fall.

Bessie Wagner
Prince Theater
Job Openings

• Artistic Intern
Unpaid internship in the artistic department in all aspects of administration and production. This person will perform assistant duties for the artistic director.

• Assistant Technical Director
Part-time position responsible for production management and stage machinery. Applicants should have related experience in stage management.

• Director of Ticket Operations
Full-time position responsible for overall management of ticket operations for all events taking place at the theater. Responsibilities include box office operations as well as planning and implementing all ticket sales processes, and supervision of the ticketing staff.

• Marketing Director
Full-time position responsible for marketing concerning all of the productions put on by the theater. Oversee the preparation of high-quality promotional materials to attract theatergoers to our plays, musicals, and concerts.

- All full-time employees of Prince Theater are eligible for complimentary access to all productions.
- All of the positions will be open starting this October.
- For more Information or to apply, contact Sam Berry by e-mail at sberry@princetheater.com.

part7.description:
April 5—Clearwater Hospital in downtown Scranton has launched a new pen pal letter-writing program between terminally ill hospital patients and adult volunteers. Hospital Director Zack Chambers, who was recently presented with an Outstanding Leader Award from the National Health Care Alliance, started the program to create stronger connections between the hospital and the community. Mr. Chambers encourages adults of all types and occupations to apply even if they don't feel completely qualified. Simply visit the Clearwater Hospital website and become a member of the hospital free of charge.

"I hope through this program, volunteers can form close relationships with patients to help them get through these difficult times in their lives," said Mr. Chambers. He also hopes that the program will lead to more people visiting terminally ill patients in person.
Clearwater Hospital
May 4

Monica Greene
4100 Washington Road
Scranton, Wisconsin 54481

Dear Ms. Greene,

I was delighted to receive your letter, I am very excited to have been paired with you as pen pals. I hope we can learn a lot from each other and build a lasting friendship.

As you know, I live in California, which is a long way from Wisconsin. 1 hope that in the coming months I can find some time off work and visit you. Please let me know when the most convenient time would be for me to meet you.

I look forward to hearing from you,
Jessica Wrigt
Dear Jessica,

You don't know how much I appreciate your kind words. Although the staff at Clearwater are very kind, I feel the need to connect with people who are not part of the staff. My surviving family also live a great distance away, in Florida, and so most of the time I am just communicating with the paid staff or the other patients. I would welcome a visit, if you truly wanted to come, and the best time would be for our meeting is the Thanksgiving holiday party here at the center I suppose. My own family might be here as well. If it is too much for you, or if you can't get the time off of work, don't worry about it too much. I do hope that we can continue to communicate through our letters.

All the best,
Monica Greene

part7.description:
Mr, John Morris
1423 Bernard Avenue
Millville, CA 90117

Dear Mr. Morris,

24/7 Fitness is the most successful workout facility in the United States, With over 3 million members nationwide, our franchise has become known as a reputable and trustworthy brand. Our success is a result of great relationships between us the franchiser and our franchisees.

You are receiving this mailing because you expressed interest in partnering with 24/7 Fitness in order to open a new location in your town. According to our preliminary research, your town has a large population of young, single people working in the professional field. This is our target demographic, and it means the business outlook for your 24/7 Fitness location is positive in your town. If you would like more information about the specific terms and regulations when partnering with 24/7 Fitness, please don't hesitate to call me at 347-555-3363. Additionally, if you would like to talk to another franchise owner, that information can be supplied by one of our associates.

Sincerely,
Lori Swanson
Chief Operating Officer
To: Zack Carter <zcarter@zenmail.com>
From: John Morris <jimorris@cbnet.com>
Subject: 24/7 Fitness
Date: March 6
Dear Mr. Carter,

My name is John Morris and I am a small business owner living in the Millville area. I am currently in negotiations with 24/7 Fitness to open my own location here in Millville. As someone who works with 24/7 Fitness, you would help me a lot by sharing your opinions.

I am interested in how you assess 24/7 Fitness as a franchiser. I operated several franchises in the past, and I always found that trust and honesty are the most important factors in a successful relationship. More importantly, I was also wondering what kind of support is provided by the parent company. Before opening your location, did you receive adequate training to allow you to smoothly begin operating your business? Any advice you can give me would be much appreciated.

Sincerely,
John Morris
To: John Morris <jmorris@cbnet.com>
From: Zack Carter <zcarter@zenmail.com>
Subject: 24/7 Fitness
Date: March 7
Dear Mr. Morris,

I am happy to provide some insight into the operation of a 24/7 Fitness franchise. I have been working with 24/7 Fitness as a franchise owner for 10 years now. I actually run three different branches now. I completely agree with you that trust and honesty are the two most important aspects of any business relationship. On that count, I believe the fact that I own three franchises is testament to my faith in the franchiser.

Let me put your mind at ease. First off, 24/7 Fitness has a very specific way that they want their brand to develop no matter who owns the branch. The parent company will not only provide training, but they insist on controlling the actual layout of the facilities from the locker rooms to the free weights. They want any of their 3 million members to be able to walk into any one of their gyms and feel at home. Until you have been operating for one full year, you must make monthly reports to corporate headquarters detailing all aspects of sales, membership, and a flow chart describing the usage of the facilities. It really is hands on until they have confidence you can represent the brand. I hope this helps you decide to join the 24/7 Fitness team!

All the best,
Zack Carter

Therefore, I am looking for a warehouse located in the outskirts of Pittsburg. The warehouse needs to be located close to the highway. We are shipping a high volume of products, so we would prefer a dedicated warehouse to be used exclusively for Turner Electronics operations. A warehouse with a spacious loading bay for large trucks is necessary. Additionally, a warehouse that also has office space would be ideal. Because of the valuable nature of our products, we would like a warehouse that provides precautions against theft and damage.

I look forward to hearing your response soon.

Steven Mason
Turner Electronics
To: Steven Mason <smason@turnerelectronics.com>
From: Kevin Scott <kevinscott@startrealty.com>
Date: February 3
Subject: Re: A warehouse
Dear Mr. Mason,

It seems that as your company expands, you would like to improve the operations of your distribution network and deliver products to sellers more quickly. We have a variety of warehouse options, and I trust one of them will fit your company's needs. All locations have a state-of-the-art security system as well as experienced staff.

Location 1—$3,499 per month for a 10,000-square-foot warehouse space shared by multiple businesses. Because this location is a shared operations site, we offer it at a discounted price.
Location 2-$5,500 per month for an older warehouse located in downtown Pittsburg. This warehouse is currently empty, and therefore can be used by your company exclusively. It also features a walk-in freezer.
Location 3-$6,500 per month for a very spacious warehouse located a few miles outside of Pittsburg. Although currently used by two other businesses as a storage space, it can be converted into a warehouse only for your company.
Location 4—$2,600 per month for a medium-size warehouse. This warehouse is provided at a discounted price because it has no area for trucks to unload cargo conveniently. It is best for smaller-sized operations.

These are the locations currently available for use. If you have any questions or would like to visit a .location in person, please contact me.

Kevin Scott
To: Kevin Scott <kevinscott@startrealty.com>
From: Steven Mason <smason@turnerelectronics.com>
Date: February 3
Subject: Location 3
Dear Mr. Scott,

Thank you so much for responding to my inquiry so quickly. Although none of the warehouses is exactly what I was looking for, I think the best option for our business will be Location 3. This, of course, is contingent on the other two businesses moving their storage into another warehouse. Our operations, as I noted in my first e-mail, are expanding, and I want to make sure that we have ample room to grow. I am delighted that there is security at your warehouses as well.

I have some time early next week if it would be possible to take a walk through Location 3. I think once I get a feel for the space, I will be able to make a firm decision. Please contact me by phone at your convenience so we can set up a time.
You can reach me at (351) 546-9899.

All the best,
Steve Mason
Turner Electronics
